Regression Learner for L0-Regularized Best Subset Selection

Source: R/LearnerRegrL0Learn.R
LearnerRegrL0Learn.Rd

Sparse linear regression with L0, L0L1 or L0L2 penalties, fitted by coordinate descent and local combinatorial search with L0Learn::L0Learn.cvfit(). The penalty parameters lambda and gamma are chosen by cross-validation inside L0Learn::L0Learn.cvfit(), then the pair with the smallest mean cross-validated error is stored in the model and used for prediction.

The loss is always the squared error. Features must be "integer" or "numeric", and missing values are not supported by L0Learn.

Initial parameter values

All parameters have the tag "train" and are passed to L0Learn::L0Learn.cvfit(), except selection, which is used by the learner itself. Parameters that are not set explicitly keep the defaults of L0Learn. nGamma, gammaMax and gammaMin only matter for the "L0L1" and "L0L2" penalties.

Cross-validation folds

The folds are built by L0Learn::L0Learn.cvfit(), which cannot split every number of rows n into every number of folds nFolds. When ceiling(n / nFolds) * (nFolds - 1) >= n it either fails with an out-of-bounds error or returns only NaN cross-validation errors. For example nFolds = 10 fails on the 32 rows of mlr3::tsk("mtcars"). The learner then stops with an informative error, and another value of nFolds must be chosen.

Random numbers

L0Learn::L0Learn.cvfit() calls set.seed(seed). The learner restores the state of the random number generator after training, so fitting it does not change the random numbers drawn afterwards. The cross-validation folds are the same for a given seed, whose default is 1.

Choice of lambda and gamma

With selection = "min" (the default) the learner uses the pair with the smallest mean cross-validated error. When several values are tied, the one furthest along the lambda path (the smallest lambda, usually the largest support) is used.

With selection = "1se" the learner keeps the gamma of that minimum, then takes the model on the lambda path with the smallest support among those whose mean cross-validated error is within one standard error of the minimum. The standard error is the standard deviation of the fold errors at the minimum divided by sqrt(nFolds). If it is not available the minimum is used, with a warning. This usually gives a smaller support and a more stable choice of features.

Bounds and custom penalty grids

lows and highs are single numbers that bound every coefficient, with lows <= 0 <= highs and lows < highs. Bounds are not supported by algorithm = "CDPSI". lambdaGrid is a list of strictly decreasing positive numeric vectors. For penalty = "L0" it must contain exactly one vector, and for "L0L1" and "L0L2" it contains one vector per value of gamma. When it is set, nLambda is ignored by L0Learn and nGamma is replaced by the number of vectors. L0Learn can drop the last values of a grid whose support exceeds maxSuppSize, so the stored path may be shorter than the grid. excludeFirstK cannot be larger than the number of features, because L0Learn would abort the R session.

Model

After training, learner$model is a list with these elements:

  • fit: the "L0LearnCV" object returned by L0Learn::L0Learn.cvfit().

  • gamma_index, lambda_index: the position of the selected pair in the regularization path of fit.

  • lambda, gamma: the selected values.

  • support_size: the number of non-zero coefficients of the selected model.

  • cv_mean, cv_sd: the mean and standard deviation, across folds, of the cross-validated error at the selected pair.

Selected features

learner$selected_features() returns the names of the features with a non-zero coefficient at the selected (lambda, gamma) pair.

References

Hazimeh H, Mazumder R (2020). "Fast Best Subset Selection: Coordinate Descent and Local Combinatorial Optimization Algorithms." Operations Research, 68(5), 1517-1537. doi:10.1287/opre.2019.1919

Examples

library(mlr3L0Learn)
learner <- mlr3::lrn("regr.L0Learn", penalty = "L0", nFolds = 5L)
task <- mlr3::tsk("mtcars")
learner$train(task)
learner$selected_features()
#> [1] "am"   "carb" "drat" "qsec" "wt"  
prediction <- learner$predict(task)
prediction$score(mlr3::msr("regr.mse"))
#> regr.mse 
#> 4.898502
